parole.significato: Forms the partitive case of nouns, adjectives, numbers and some pronouns.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-da (variant of *-ta, whence -ta), from the Proto-Uralic ablative case *-ta.

parole.significato: Used for forming nouns from verbs or adjectives.
parole.testo: Conflated: * Proto-Finnic *-ëk, from Proto-Uralic *-ek * Proto-Finnic *-ëh, from Proto-Uralic *-eš; cognate with Proto-Samic *-ës Historically, *-ëk was deverbal, while *-ëh was denominal.

parole.significato: A suffix for making adjectives from some nouns and verbs.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-ëda, from Proto-Uralic *-(e)ta.

parole.significato: Forms frequentative verbs. The resulting verb often describes a more or less leisurely or long-lasting activity, or an…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-(ë)ldak, from Proto-Uralic *-le-.

parole.significato: Forms translative verbs from adjectives, meaning "to become (adjective)" or "to become more (adjective)".
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-t'ak (stem *-në-), from Proto-Uralic *-me-. Related to Estonian -nema, -neda and Veps -eta. The stem has been reworked considerably in some forms; see the Proto-Finnic entry for more details.

From Proto-Finnic *-hën, a variant of *-sën, probably related to *-lën (allative case suffix) and composed of -s- (internal locative suffix; see -ssa) + Proto-Uralic *-ŋ (lative or dative suffix) (with an epenthetic *-e-). The preceding vowel began to assimilate the vowel in the suffix.

parole.significato: A non-productive nominal suffix deriving nouns from nominal stems.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-i, from Proto-Uralic *-j (specifically its fusion with the stem vowel). Originally allomorphic with -o (< *-oi, in which the *-i- caused labialization of the preceding *a). In many derived suffixes, both variants can be seen, such as in -kki, -kko, both from < *-kka-i. The former
Conflated: * from Proto-Finnic *-i (from Proto-Uralic *-j (lative suffix)) * from *-ik (from earlier *-jek, probably a combination of the aforementioned and Proto-Uralic *-k (lative suffix)).

parole.significato: Plural marker in nominal forms, except in nominative case, in which it is -t.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-i-, from Proto-Uralic *-j (oblique plural marker).
From Proto-Finnic *-i-, from Proto-Uralic *-j (past tense marker).

parole.significato: Forms primarily transitive verbs describing repeating (frequentative) or continuous (continuative) action.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-idak, from Proto-Uralic *-j-.

parole.significato: Forms inanimate instrumental nouns from verbs.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-in (instrumental suffix), probably from Proto-Uralic *-ma.
From Proto-Finnic *-in (superlative suffix) (related to Karelian -in), probably from Proto-Uralic *-ma. The oblique stem -impA, -immA is influenced by the oblique stem -mpA, -mmA of comparatives.

parole.significato: A suffix for making adjectives from some nouns and verbs.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-isa, possibly from Proto-Uralic. Related to Estonian -s (such as in jõudus (gen. jõudsa) ~ joutuisa), Ingrian -isa, Votic -zõ.

From Proto-Finnic *-it'ak, from Proto-Uralic *-ńće-, *-nśe- (probably akin to the diminutive ending -ise-). The original stem before preceding endings other than original *-et-, is *-icc- (e.g. *valic'en, *valiccepi, but *valit'ak). However, potential forms were replaced with ones in -nn- by semi-re

parole.significato: A diminutive suffix. No longer productive.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-icca, from Proto-Uralic [Term?]. Cognate with Livvi -čču.

parole.significato: Forms agent nouns, especially human ones; -er
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-ja (agent noun suffix), from Proto-Uralic *-ja (present participle ending).

parole.significato: functionally a conjunction, suffixed to the negation verb to join two main clauses; and (not) (see eikä)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-ka, from Proto-Uralic *-ka. Originally probably an emphatic particle.

parole.significato: Turns a clause interrogative. It is appended to the element of the clause that is questioned most. English equivalents…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-ko, probably ultimately from Proto-Uralic *ko-.

parole.significato: used to form the translative case
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-ksi, from Proto-Uralic *-kse. Related to Erzya -кс (-ks, translative suffix) and Moksha -кс (-ks, translative suffix).

parole.significato: forms the allative case of a noun, adjective, numeral or pronoun
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-(l)lëk, a variant of *-(l)lën (whence dialectal -len, -llen), which is related to *-sën (illative case suffix) and is composed of -l(l)- (external locative suffix) + Proto-Uralic *-ŋ (lative or dative suffix) (with an epenthetic *-e-). Compare Erzya and Moksha -нень (-neń, allati
From Proto-Finnic *-ma, from Proto-Uralic *-ma (compare Moksha -ма (-ma) in эряма (eŕama, “life”), кулома (kuloma, “death”)).

parole.significato: The suffix of the agent participle.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-ma, from Proto-Uralic *-ma.

parole.significato: Forms the first-person plural of verbs.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-kma (< *-k-ma), from *-k (marker for the present tense) + *-ma (from Proto-Uralic). Form influenced by me, the first-person plural personal pronoun. In the past tense, there was originally -i- in place of -k- (*-ima > *-imë), but the present suffix has been generalized to all ten

parole.significato: Used to form the genitive case.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-n, conflated from Proto-Uralic *-n (genitive suffix) and from Proto-Uralic *-m (accusative suffix).

parole.significato: the first-person singular suffix for verbs
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-n, from Proto-Uralic *-m, probably connected to the first-person singular personal pronoun minä.
From Proto-Finnic *-na, from the Proto-Uralic locative case ending *-na.

parole.significato: Marker of potential mood in verbs.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-në-, probably from Proto-Uralic *-ne. Related to Ingrian -ne-, Karelian -ne-, Votic -ne-, and probably Hungarian -na-, -ne- (conditional mood markers).

parole.significato: First-person singular possessive suffix used with or without minun (the genitive of the personal pronoun minä), corresp…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-ni, from Proto-Uralic *-ne. Originally *-mi was the first-person singular possessive suffix used in the nominative singular, but -ni has replaced it, and it is now only found in dialects. Compare Erzya -м (-m).

parole.significato: The second-person plural possessive suffix. Used when addressing many persons or one person in a polite or formal manne…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-ndak (originally the oblique/plural possessive ending with a second-person plural possessor), from Proto-Uralic *-nta[t/k]. The vowel is influenced by the second-person plural pronouns like te. Cognates include Moksha and Erzya -нк (-nk).

parole.significato: Third-person possessive suffix, used with the genitive forms of the third-person pronouns hän sg (hänen) and he pl (hei…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-nsak, from Proto-Uralic *-nsa[t/k]. In Finnic, this was a third-person plural oblique possessive suffix (i.e. for a third-person plural possessor and all cases except the nominative singular). Third-person singular and plural possessive forms merged quite early on. Adopted in wes

parole.significato: Forms nouns that describe an action.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-nta, from Proto-Uralic *-nta. Related to Karelian -nta, Livvi -ndu and Veps -nd, as well as to Estonian -nd, possibly borrowed from Finnish.

parole.significato: Forms factitive verbs from adjectives and names of languages, meaning "causing to become" or "making"; -en, -fy
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-ntadak, possibly even from Proto-Uralic *-mta-, but in any case equal to -(e)n(e)- + -taa (the causative form of -eta, with which the stem-final vowel change is shared).

parole.significato: Forms result or action nouns from verbs.
parole.testo: Conflated: * from Proto-Finnic *-o (forms action/result nouns), from Proto-Uralic *-w (originally as applied to stems ending in -a). * from Proto-Finnic *-oi (variant/diminutive), from Proto-Uralic *-j (diminutive ending), Originally, the -j labialized the preceding -a- when appended to an a-stem, r

parole.significato: Forms frequentative and continuative verbs, primarily from nouns or verbs ending in -ta or -ata, but also from adverbs.
parole.testo: Conflated: * from Proto-Finnic *-odak, from Proto-Uralic *-w- (as applied to stems ending in -a-, compare -o). * from Proto-Finnic *-oidak, from Proto-Uralic *-j- (like in *-idak, -ia, as applied to stems ending in -a-, compare -o; the -o- is a re-extraction from the suffix being applied to stems en

parole.significato: Forms ordinal numbers from cardinal numbers, or ordinal pronouns.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-nci, from Proto-Uralic *-mte.

parole.significato: Second-person singular possessive suffix used with or without sinun (the genitive form of the personal pronoun sinä): y…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-ci, from Proto-Uralic *-te. Compare Erzya -т (-t).

parole.significato: Forms the nominative and accusative plural.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-t, from Proto-Uralic *-t.

parole.significato: Forms the second person singular of verbs.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-t, from Proto-Uralic *-t, probably related to second-person pronouns *tinä, *te.

parole.significato: Forms verbs from nouns, generally with a causative, factitive or instrumental meaning.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-t'ak, from Proto-Uralic *-ta- (verbalizer) (see the Proto-Finnic entry for more).

parole.significato: A suffix for the partitive singular case.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-ta, ultimately from the Proto-Uralic ablative case *-ta (compare to Moksha -да, -та (-da, -ta) and Erzya -до (-do)).
From Proto-Finnic *-tadak, from Proto-Uralic *-ta- (verbalizer).

parole.significato: Indicates lack of something; -less, un-, in-, non-, -free.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-t'oin (compare Estonian -tu), from Proto-Uralic *-ktama (compare Northern Sami -heapme and Moksha -фтома (-ftoma), Erzya -(в)томо (-(v)tomo), Udmurt -тэм (-tem)).

parole.significato: Suffix for the abessive case: without
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-tta, from Proto-Uralic *-pta.

parole.significato: Forms causative verbs from verbs and nominals.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-ttadak, from Proto-Uralic *-kta-, *-pta- (conflated).

parole.significato: Forms the second-person plural of verbs.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-kta (< *-k-ta), from *-k (marker for the present tense) + *-ta (from Proto-Uralic). Form influenced by te, the second-person plural personal pronoun. In the past tense, there was originally -i- in place of -k- (*-ita > *-itë), but the present suffix has been generalized to all te

parole.significato: Forms nouns from verbs. Most common with e- and i-stem verbs.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-u, from Proto-Uralic *-w (originally as applied to stems ending in -e or -ä). Cognate with Estonian -u.

parole.significato: Forms passive (including stative) or translative (including inchoative) intransitive verbs from transitive verbs.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-udak, from Proto-Uralic *-w-. Cognates include Estonian -uma/-uda.

parole.significato: Forms the present active participle of a verb, which is normally used like an adjective. The English equivalent is norm…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *-pa, from Proto-Uralic *-pa. The weak-grade variant *-ba was eventually extended by analogy to all verbs. The original strong grade remains as -pa in a few words (e.g. syöpä, käypä, kaikkivoipa), but these have lost their verbal meaning.
From Proto-Finnic *-k, from Proto-Uralic *-k.

parole.significato: akja, large pulk (low-slung boat-like sled), suitable for carrying goods or people in deep snow, usually drawn by a man…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic [Term?] (compare Karelian ahkivo), possibly from Proto-Uralic *aškɜ (compare Northern Khanty өхәԓ (øhəł)). The narrow distribution in just northern Finnish dialects and Karelian could also imply a Sami intermediate, but no related Sami words appear to exist (akio, akia are apparent

parole.significato: to cram, stuff, fill, pack full
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *aktadak (“to hang up to dry, to fill a grain-drying cabin”), from Proto-Uralic *ëkta- (“to hang up, to set up a trap”) (compare Moksha афтомс (aftoms, “to set a trap, to cast a net”), Northern Khanty ихәт (ihət, “to hang up (to dry, etc.)”), Tundra Nenets ӈыдась (ŋidasʹ°, “to hang
From Proto-Finnic *aita (compare Estonian aed, Karelian aita /aida, Livvi aidu), from Proto-Uralic *ajta (compare Northern Khanty ощ (osj)).
From Proto-Finnic *aivo (compare Estonian aju (“brain, mind”)), from Proto-Uralic *ajŋe (compare Hungarian agy (“brain”) and possibly Moksha уй (uj, “brain”)).

parole.significato: to drive, ride, travel (in a vehicle), transport (e.g. in a car)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ajadak (compare Estonian ajama), from Proto-Uralic *aja- (compare Northern Sami vuodjit, Udmurt уйыны (ujyny), Eastern Mansi [script needed] (wujt-)). Probably an old borrowing from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eǵ- or one of its descendants; see the Proto-Uralic entry for more.

From Proto-Finnic *ala (compare Estonian ala-), from Proto-Uralic *ëla (compare Northern Sami vuolli, Erzya ало (alo), Eastern Mari ӱлан (ülan), Udmurt ул (ul), Eastern Khanty ыл (yl), Hungarian al-, Tundra Nenets ӈылʼ (ŋil)).

parole.significato: to begin, start, initiate, set in, be initiated, originate, be originated, take its origin
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *alkadak (compare Estonian algama), possibly from Proto-Uralic *alka- (“to begin”) (compare Northern Mansi о̄вл (ōvl, “head”)).

parole.significato: something that widens on a mouth section, like a mouth or a cavity
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ammo, from Proto-Uralic *aŋma-w. Cognate to Ingrian ammillaa, Votic ammulla, Estonian ammuli, Estonian ammu, Livonian amtlõ (“to yawn”), Skolt Sami ämmsõddâd (“to yawn”), Western Mari [script needed] (omeštaš, “to talk or move while in sleep or to talk unclearly”), Southern Selkup

parole.significato: Very long ago, in the time immemorial.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ammo- (compare Estonian ammu (“once upon a time, long ago”)), probably from Proto-Uralic *amme (“old, previous”) + -oin (temporal singular) (compare Northern Sami oamis (“past, old”), Erzya умок (umok, “a long time ago”), Hungarian ó (“ancient, in previous”)).
From Proto-Finnic *anoppi (compare Veps anopʹ), from Proto-Uralic *ënɜppe (compare Tundra Nenets ӈынаб (ŋinab°)).

parole.significato: to give [with allative ‘to’] (transfer possession of to someone else)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *antadak (compare Estonian andma), from Proto-Uralic *amta- (compare Northern Sami vuovdit (“to sell”), Erzya андомс (andoms, “to feed”), Eastern Mari омдеш (omdeš), Komi-Zyrian удны (udny), Hungarian ad).

From Proto-Finnic *appadak (compare Estonian apama, Karelian appoa, Veps apta), from Proto-Uralic *appa- (compare Northern Sami vuohpput, Eastern Mari уваш (uvaš), Tundra Nenets [script needed] (ŋabə[r]-)).
From Proto-Finnic *appi, from Proto-Uralic *ëppe (compare Northern Sami vuohppa, archaic Hungarian ipa).
From Proto-Finnic *asëdak, from Proto-Uralic *ëśe-.

parole.significato: step, pace (advance or movement made from one foot to the other)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *askël (compare Livvi askel), from Proto-Uralic *aśkele ~ *aśka-le (compare Erzya эскелькс (eskeľks), Eastern Mari ошкыл (oškyl), Komi-Zyrian воськов (vośkov), Northern Mansi ӯсыл (ūsyl)).
From Proto-Finnic *asudak, from Proto-Uralic *ëśew-. Equivalent to asea + -ua.

parole.significato: The negative verb or negation verb; not, be not, do not, etc.
parole.testo: The indicative forms are from Proto-Finnic *e-, from Proto-Uralic *e- (negative verb stem). The imperative forms are from Proto-Finnic *älä-, from the Proto-Finno-Ugric negative imperative verb stem *älä- ~ *elä-. Details and cognates Noteworthy forms include eivät (replacing earlier evät by influen
From Proto-Finnic *ellä, from Proto-Uralic *e- (“this”) + -llä (adessive case marker).
From Proto-Finnic *eläbä, from Proto-Uralic *eläpä. Equivalent to elää (“to live”) + -vä (present active participle).
From Proto-Finnic *elädäk (compare Estonian elama), from Proto-Uralic *elä- (compare Northern Sami eallit, Eastern Mari илаш (ilaš), Hungarian él, Tundra Nenets илесь (yilyesʹ°)).

From Proto-Finnic *emä (compare Estonian ema), from Proto-Uralic *emä (compare Hungarian eme (“sow”), Tundra Nenets небя (nyebya)). Mostly displaced in the sense “mother (of a person)” by the borrowed äiti.
From Proto-Finnic *enä, from Proto-Uralic *enä (compare Skolt Sami jõnn, Erzya ине (ine, “large, great”)).
From Proto-Finnic *es, derived from Proto-Uralic *e- (“this”) (the same root as in että) + -s. Cognate with obsolete Võro es (“if, (even) though”).
From Proto-Finnic *eci (compare Estonian esi), from Proto-Uralic *ede (compare Northern Mansi эла (èla), Hungarian elé).

parole.significato: that (conjunction indicating that the subordinate clause is the object of the verb of the main clause)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *että, from Proto-Uralic *e- (“this”) + -tta (suffix indicating manner). Cognate with Estonian et, Erzya эте (ete), while the Uralic root is also found in Hungarian ez. According to Häkkinen (2004), the original sense was probably “like this, thus”; semantic influence from the simi

parole.significato: A single hair, especially a grey hair of an ageing person.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hapci, possibly from Proto-Uralic *ëpte (but see the Proto-Finnic entry for more).
From Proto-Finnic *harva (compare Estonian harv, Ingrian harva), from Proto-Uralic [Term?] (compare Erzya чуро (čuro, “rare, sparse”) and Southern Khanty турәп (turəp, “sparse”)).

parole.significato: mouse (used rather indiscriminately for a number of small mouse-resembling rodents mostly in the zoologic family Murida…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hiiri (compare Estonian hiir), from Proto-Uralic *šiŋere (compare Erzya чеерь (čejeŕ), Northern Mansi таӈкер (taňker), Hungarian egér). * (computer mouse): Semantic loan from English mouse.

parole.significato: lip, labium (either of the two fleshy protrusions around the opening of the mouth)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *huuli (compare Estonian huul, Veps hulʹ, Votic uuli), from Proto-Uralic *šuwle (compare Eastern Khanty лул (lul)).
From Proto-Finnic *igen (compare Estonian ige), from Proto-Uralic *jiken (compare Hungarian íny).

parole.significato: marvel, wonder, prodigy (something that causes amazement or awe)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *imeh (compare Estonian ime, Votic ime, Karelian imeh), derived from Proto-Uralic *jemä (compare Northern Sami amas, Northern Khanty йєм (jêm, “prohibited; sacred”)).
From Proto-Finnic *iho (compare Estonian ihu), probably from Proto-Uralic *iša (compare Moksha ёжа (joža, “skin”), Erzya ёжо (jožo, “surface”)).

parole.significato: age (time which someone or something has been alive or existed)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ikä (compare Estonian iga), from Proto-Uralic *jekä (compare Northern Sami jahki, Erzya ие (ije, “year”), Eastern Mari ий (ij), Hungarian év).
From Proto-Finnic *ilma (“air, sky, weather”), from Proto-Uralic *jilma (“sky, weather, god”).
From Proto-Finnic *imedäk (compare Estonian imema, Karelian imie), from Proto-Uralic *ime- (compare Hungarian emik).

parole.significato: oneself, itself (used to emphasize the person or thing acting as the headword)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *icek ~ *ic'ek (compare Estonian ise), from Proto-Uralic *iće (compare Northern Sami ieš, Erzya эсь (eś, “own, oneself”), Eastern Mari шке (ške), Udmurt ачим (aćim), Northern Mansi [script needed] (is), Northern Khanty ис (is, “soul”)). The original meaning in Proto-Uralic was “sha
From Proto-Finnic *itä, from Proto-Uralic *itä- (“to appear”) (whence also itää); the sun rises (appears) in the east.
From Proto-Finnic *itädäk, from Proto-Uralic *itä- (“to appear, become visible”) (compare Northern Khanty єтты (êtty, “to grow”), Nganasan ӈәтәдя (ŋətədja)).

parole.significato: to divide, split into parts, cut up
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jakadak (compare Estonian jagama), from Proto-Uralic *jëk(k)a- ~ *jak(k)a- (compare Northern Sami juohkit, Erzya явомс (javoms), Udmurt люкыны (ľukyny) and possibly Tundra Nenets яхӑсь (yaxăsʹ°)).

parole.significato: foot, leg; a lower supporting limb of a human or animal
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jalka (compare Estonian jalg, Livonian jālga), from Proto-Uralic *jalka (compare Northern Sami juolgi, Erzya ялго (jalgo, “on foot”), Eastern Mari йол (jol), Hungarian gyalog (“on foot”)).

parole.significato: river (large stream which drains a landmass)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *joki (compare Estonian jõgi (“river”), Karelian joki /jogi (“river”), Veps jogi (“river”)), from Proto-Uralic *joke (compare Northern Sami johka, Moksha Йов (Jov, “Moksha river”), Northern Mansi я̄ (â̄, “river”), archaic Hungarian jó).

parole.significato: transom, putlog (horizontal or transverse beam of scaffolding that is perpendicular to a wall)
parole.testo: From earlier jotka, possibly from Proto-Finnic *jotka (without any Finnic cognates), if from Proto-Uralic [Term?] (compare Erzya [script needed] (jutko, “gap”), Moksha [script needed] (jutka), [script needed] (jotka, “gap”), Southern Mansi [script needed] (jät, “middle”), Eastern Mansi [script neede

From Proto-Finnic *jousi (“bow”), from Proto-Uralic *joŋse (compare Erzya ёнкс (jonks, “bow”), Northern Mansi ё̄вт (jōvt, “bow”), Hungarian íj (“bow”), Tundra Nenets ӈын (ŋin°)). * (unit of taxation): Supposedly originally a tax based on the number of men who were strong enough to cock a crossbow (l

From Proto-Finnic *joodak (compare Estonian jooma), from Proto-Uralic *jëxe- (compare Northern Sami juhkat, Komi-Zyrian юны (juny), Northern Mansi аюӈкве (aûňkve), Hungarian iszik, Tundra Nenets ӈэ̇рпӑсь (ŋėrpăsʹ°)).
From Proto-Finnic *joostak, possibly from Proto-Uralic.
From Proto-Finnic *juttu (compare Estonian jutt), from Proto-Uralic *jupta- (“to speak, to tell”) + -u (compare Erzya ёвтамс (jovtams, “to say, to tell a story”), Nganasan дебтудя (djebtudja)).
Derived from Proto-Finnic *jürädäk, probably from Proto-Uralic *jürä-. The nature of the suffix -si- is uncertain (? < *-ci- < *-tV-i-, containing the ancestors of Finnish -ta- and -i-).

parole.significato: track, trail (mark left as a sign of passage of a person or animal)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jälki (compare Estonian jälg), from Proto-Uralic *jälke (compare Hungarian jel).
From Proto-Finnic *jändek (compare Veps jände), from Proto-Uralic *jänte(ŋ) (compare Eastern Mari йыдаҥ (jydaŋ), Eastern Khanty јӫнтӛɣ, Tundra Nenets ен (yen°)).

From Proto-Finnic *kaiho (“harm, damage, loss”) (compare Estonian kahju, Ingrian kaiho, Livonian ka’j), from Proto-Uralic *kajša-w (“sickness”). Compare Erzya кажо (kažo, “misfortune, disaster”).

parole.significato: to dig, dig up, dig out, excavate
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kaivadak (compare Estonian kaevama), from Proto-Uralic *kajwa- (compare Northern Sami goaivut, Komi-Zyrian койны (kojny, “to pour”), Tundra Nenets сива (syiwa, “shovel”)).
From Proto-Finnic *kajaga (compare Estonian kajakas, Veps kajag and Votic kajagõ), possibly from Proto-Uralic *kaja.

From Proto-Finnic *kakci (compare Estonian kaks), from Proto-Uralic *käktä ~ *kakta (compare Northern Sami guoktẹ, Erzya кавто (kavto), Eastern Mari кок (kok), Komi-Zyrian кык (kyk), Northern Khanty кӑт (kăt), Hungarian két, Tundra Nenets сидя (syidya)).
From Proto-Finnic *kala (compare Estonian kala), from Proto-Uralic *kala (compare Northern Sami guolli, Erzya кал (kal), Eastern Mari кол (kol), Hungarian hal, Tundra Nenets халя (xalya)).

parole.significato: stiff (rigid, hard to bend, inflexible; e.g. of body parts that are more rigid than usual)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kankëda, possibly from Proto-Uralic *kënka-, *kënke-, whence Erzya канкстомомс (kankstomoms, “to stiffen; to get numb”).

parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kanta (compare Estonian kand), from Proto-Uralic *kënta (compare Erzya кандо (kando, “log, load”), Moksha канда (kanda), Northern Khanty ҳонт (ḥont), Northern Mansi [script needed] (χānta)). * (position, opinion, point of view, stance): Coined by Finnish physician and translator W

From Proto-Finnic *kasi, from Proto-Uralic *käsä.

parole.significato: who; (when followed by a modifier in the elative case) which one (of)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ken (compare Votic čen), from Proto-Uralic *ke (compare Ter Sami kie, Erzya ки (ki), кие (kije), Udmurt кин (kin), Hungarian ki).
From Proto-Finnic *kepedä, probably from Proto-Uralic *kepä (whence also keveä).

parole.significato: The thin outer layer of skin.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *keci, from Proto-Uralic *kete.

From Proto-Finnic *keeli (compare Estonian keel, Karelian kieli), from Proto-Uralic *käle (compare Northern Sami giella, Erzya кель (keľ), Moksha кяль (käľ), Udmurt кыл (kyl), Eastern Khanty кӧԓ (köł), Nganasan сиәде (siədje)).

parole.significato: to roll, roll over (revolve by turning over and over, turn around one's own axis, either in place or in motion)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *keeridäk, probably from Proto-Uralic *käre-.

From Proto-Finnic *kiima (compare Estonian kiim, Karelian kiima, Veps kim), from Proto-Uralic *kixe-ma, derived from *kixe- (compare Northern Sami gihkat, Northern Khanty [script needed] (koj-), Northern Mansi [script needed] (kaj-), Hungarian kéj).
From Proto-Finnic *kiiski, possibly from Proto-Uralic *kiśkɜ.
From Proto-Finnic *kiro, from Proto-Uralic *kira-(w-).

parole.significato: to suffer pain (particularly on the brink of death)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kitudak, possibly derived from Proto-Uralic *kiče (“illness”).
From Proto-Finnic *koi, from Proto-Uralic *koje.
From Proto-Finnic *koiras, from Proto-Uralic *kojera (the same root as in koira (“dog”)).

parole.significato: birch (deciduous tree of the genus Betula)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *koivu (compare Livonian kȭvaz, Veps koiv), probably from Proto-Uralic *kojwa (compare Erzya килей (kilej), Eastern Mari куэ (kue), Northern Mansi ха̄ль (hālʹ), Tundra Nenets хо (xo)).

parole.significato: to experience, trial, undergo; to suffer
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kokëdak (“to (go) see/check”) (compare Livonian ko’gtõ), probably from Proto-Uralic *koke- (“to see/check”) (compare Tundra Nenets хось (xosʹ°)). The original meaning of this word was probably “to (go) check (a fishing net)”, from which the more abstract senses have developed.

parole.significato: traditional type of knapsack made of birch bark
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kontti, possibly from Proto-Uralic *konte. Cognate to Karelian kontti and Livonian kōņtad (“testicles”).
From Proto-Finnic *kontti, possibly from Proto-Uralic *konte. Cognate to Estonian kont (“bone”).
From Proto-Finnic *koppa, possibly from Proto-Uralic *koppa. Originally meant hollow.

parole.significato: to annoy, irritate, vex; (impersonal) to be annoyed, irritated, vexed
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *korbët'ak, from Proto-Uralic *korpe-. Cognates include Erzya курвамс (kurvams) and possibly Hungarian hervad.

parole.significato: rapid(s) (a rough section of a river or stream)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *koski, from Proto-Uralic *kośke.

parole.significato: moment, short while (short period of time)

From Proto-Finnic *kumma, probably from Proto-Uralic *kumma ~ *kumɜ (“shady, dark”).

parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kumpu, from Proto-Uralic *kumpe (“elevation, hillock”), whence also Erzya кумбо (kumbo, “hummock”), Moksha комба (komba, “hump”) and Proto-Samic *kompë. Contains a -u suffix which is not seen in the earlier derivation kumpare.

From Proto-Finnic *kooldak (compare Livonian kūolõ, Veps kolda), from Proto-Uralic *kale- (compare Erzya куломс (kuloms), Eastern Mari колаш (kolaš), Komi-Zyrian кувны (kuvny), Northern Mansi хо̄луӈкве (hōluňkve), Hungarian hal, Tundra Nenets хась (xasʹ°)).
Uncertain. Possibly from Proto-Finnic *koona, from Proto-Uralic *kane ~ *kana. Related to Karelian kuona.

Related to Russian ко́рюшка (kórjuška), likely a Finnic or earl
From Proto-Finnic *kuras, from Proto-Uralic *kurɜ. Cognates include Estonian kuurask, Karelian kuras, Votic kuraz, Lule Sami gürra and Tundra Nenets хар (xər°).
From Proto-Finnic *kurki, from Proto-Uralic *kurke, itself an onomatopoeic word. Cognates include Estonian kurg, Northern Sami guorga and Erzya карго (kargo).
From Proto-Finnic *kusi, from Proto-Uralic *kuńśe. Cognates include Northern Sami gužža and Hungarian húgy.

From Proto-Finnic *kuu, from Proto-Uralic *kuŋe. Cognates include Estonian kuu, Erzya ков (kov) and Hungarian hold.

parole.significato: spruce (any tree in the genus Picea)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kuusi (compare Estonian kuusk), from Proto-Uralic *kowse (compare Northern Sami guossa, Erzya куз (kuz), Eastern Mari кож (kož), Udmurt кыз (kyz), Tundra Nenets хады (xadi)).

parole.significato: village (rural habitation smaller than a town)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *külä (compare Estonian küla), from Proto-Uralic *külä (“dwelling”) (compare Northern Sami gallet (“to visit”), Northern Mansi кол (kol, “house”)). First attested in 1330 in the place name Ylyskølum.
From Proto-Finnic *künci (compare Estonian küüs), from Proto-Uralic *künče (compare Ter Sami kannc, Erzya кенже (kenže), Hungarian köröm).

parole.significato: to hook, hook up, connect, couple
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kütkedäk, from Proto-Uralic *kütke- (compare Eastern Mari кычкаш (kyčkaš), Udmurt кыткыны (kytkyny), Hungarian köt).

parole.significato: tear, teardrop (drop of clear, salty liquid produced from the eyes by crying or irritation)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *küünel, from Proto-Uralic *küńele. Cognates include Karelian kyynäl, Northern Sami ganjal, Hungarian könny.

From Proto-Finnic *küünärä, from Proto-Uralic *küńä. Cognates include Estonian küünar, Livonian kīndõr, Northern Sami gardnjil, Erzya кенере (kenere), Komi-Permyak гырддза (gyrddźa, “elbow”), the initial component of Udmurt гырпум (gyrpum, “elbow”) and Hungarian könyök.

parole.significato: sister-in-law (sister of one's spouse; wife of one's sibling)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kälü (compare Estonian käli, Karelian käly), from Proto-Uralic *kälew (compare Moksha [script needed] (ḱel), Komi-Zyrian кев (kev), Tundra Nenets сел (syel°)).

parole.significato: palm (inner, concave part of hand; corresponding part of the forefoot of a lower mammal)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kämmen (compare Estonian kämmal, Veps kämen), possibly from Proto-Uralic *kämmen.
From Proto-Finnic *käskedäk, from Proto-Uralic *käske-.
From Proto-Finnic *kätkedäk (compare Estonian kätkema), from Proto-Uralic *kätke- (compare Northern Sami gietkat, Tundra Nenets седӑсь (syedăsʹ°)).

parole.significato: to wrap (put something inside a wrapper)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kääridäk (compare Estonian käärima, Ingrian kääriä, Karelian kiärie, Veps kärdä, Votic čääriä; further also with Samic cognates, like Ter Sami кӣррэд (kīrred), possibly from Proto-Uralic *käre-.
From Proto-Finnic *keüci (compare Estonian köis), from Proto-Uralic *käwde (compare Komi-Zyrian кӧв (köv), Northern Mansi ква̄лыг (kvālyg)).

parole.significato: pond (inland body of standing water, usually natural, that is smaller than a lake)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lampi, from Proto-Uralic *lëmpe.
From Proto-Finnic *lanci, from Proto-Uralic *lënte. Cognates include Erzya ландямс (lanďams, “to squat”).

parole.significato: shoulder (the region around the shoulder blade)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lapa, from Proto-Uralic *lapa.

parole.significato: child (person who is below the age of adulthood)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lapci (compare Estonian laps), probably from Proto-Uralic *lëpće (“cradle”) (compare Erzya лавсь (lavś, “cradle”), Eastern Mari лепш (ĺepš, “cradle”), Tundra Nenets ебц (yebc°, “cradle”)).
From Proto-Finnic *latta-, possibly from Proto-Uralic *lapta.

parole.significato: broth, stock, liquor (water in which food, such as meat or vegetables, has been boiled)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *leemi (compare Estonian leem), from Proto-Uralic *läme (compare Northern Sami liepma, Erzya лем (lem, “fat”), Eastern Mari лем (ĺem), Udmurt лым (lym), Hungarian lé, Tundra Nenets евэй (yewey°)).

parole.significato: to move, stir (change places, change one's location or position)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *liikkudak (compare Estonian liikuma, Livonian likkõ, Veps likuda), possibly from Proto-Uralic *likke-(w-).

parole.significato: to read (interpret or speak aloud something written)

parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *luta (compare Estonian luda, Ingrian luta), possibly from Proto-Uralic *luča, or borrowed from Proto-Germanic *slutą (whence English slot). Also cognate with Proto-Samic *lotē.

parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *luu, from Proto-Uralic *luwe.

parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lük'äit'äk (“to push, shove”) (compare Estonian lükkama (“to push”), Veps lükäita (“to throw, push, leave”)), from Proto-Uralic *lükkä-. parole.significato: to leave, go, go away, set off, take off, depart, embark, sail
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *läktedäk (compare Livonian lǟ’dõ, Veps lähtta), from Proto-Uralic *läkte- (compare Skolt Sami liõhttâd, Eastern Mari лекташ (ĺektaš, “to leave, travel”), Udmurt лыктыны (lyktyny, “to come”), Eastern Khanty [script needed] (Liɣwǝt-)).
From Proto-Finnic *lämbin, from Proto-Uralic *lämpe (compare Moksha лямбе (lämbe)).

parole.significato: hole (usually for ventilation; depending on location) window, shutter, door
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *läpi, probably from Proto-Uralic [Term?] (compare Eastern Mari леп (ĺep)).

parole.significato: ground, land (surface of the Earth, especially that which is not covered by water)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *maa (compare Estonian maa, Karelian mua), from Proto-Uralic *mëxe (compare Komi-Zyrian му (mu), Udmurt му (mu), Northern Mansi ма̄ (mā)). Further also probably cognate with the initial component of Erzya мастор (mastor).

From Proto-Finnic *maksa (compare Estonian maks), from Proto-Uralic *mëksa (compare Skolt Sami mueksie, Erzya максо (makso), Eastern Mari мокш (mokš), Komi-Permyak мус (mus), Northern Mansi ма̄йт (mājt), Hungarian máj, Tundra Nenets мыд (mid°)).
From Proto-Finnic *matka (compare Ingrian matka, Veps matk), from Proto-Uralic *mëtka (compare Northern Sami muotki, Eastern Khanty мугәт (mugət), Northern Selkup мыты (myty) (Taz)).
From Proto-Finnic *mek, from Proto-Uralic *me. The word is inflected as plural, but there is no plural marker in the nominative, except in dialects (met).

parole.significato: to go [with illative of third infinitive ‘to do’] (move away from a point of reference)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *mendäk (compare Estonian minema, Karelian männä), from Proto-Uralic *mene- (compare Northern Sami mannat, Eastern Mari мияш (mijaš), Komi-Zyrian мунны (munny), Northern Mansi минуӈкве (minuňkve), Hungarian megy (men-), Tundra Nenets минзь (myinzʹ°)).

From Proto-Finnic *muistadak (compare Estonian mõistma (“to understand”)), probably from Proto-Uralic *muja- (compare Erzya муемс (mujems, “to find”), Eastern Mari муаш (muaš, “to find”)).
The illative singular of muka-, from Proto-Finnic *muka-, probably from Proto-Uralic *muka (“back”).
From Proto-Finnic *muna (“egg; ? penis, testes”), from Proto-Uralic *muna (“egg; ? penis, testes”).

parole.significato: mire, mud; decaying organic matter in the bottom of a lake, etc.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *muta, from Proto-Uralic *muďa. Cognate with Estonian muda, Veps muda, Karelian muta, Erzya мода (moda).
From Proto-Finnic *mura- (from which cognates are variously derived), from Proto-Uralic *mura.

From Proto-Finnic *müüdäk ~ *möödäk (compare Estonian müüma, Karelian myyvvä, Veps möda, Võro müümä), from Proto-Uralic *mixe- (“to give”) (compare Erzya миемс (mijems); see the Proto-Uralic entry for more).
From Proto-Finnic *nato, from Proto-Uralic *nataw.

parole.significato: maiden, maid (girl or young, unmarried woman)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *näitoi, derived from Proto-Uralic *näxe-.

parole.significato: to swallow, ingest (continuously or more slowly, compare nielaista and nieleskellä)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *neeldäk (compare Estonian neelama), from Proto-Uralic *ńäle- (compare Northern Sami njiellat, Erzya нилемс (nilems), Eastern Mari нелаш (ńelaš), Komi-Zyrian ньывны (ńyvny), Hungarian nyel).

From Proto-Finnic *nimi (compare Estonian nimi), from Proto-Uralic *nime (compare Northern Sami namma, Erzya лем (lem), Eastern Mari лӱм (lüm), Komi-Zyrian ним (ńim), Hungarian név, Tundra Nenets нюмʼ (nyum)); see the Proto-Uralic entry for more.

parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nisä, possibly from Proto-Uralic *ńimśä. Related to Estonian nisa, Veps ńiža and Votic nisä.

parole.significato: beak, bill, rostrum (anatomical structure of birds)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nokka (compare Estonian nokk, Karelian n'okka, Votic nokkõ), possibly from Proto-Uralic *nokka.

parole.significato: to fetch, retrieve, (go) pick up, (come) get
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *noutadak, from Proto-Uralic *ńoxe-.

From Proto-Finnic *nooli (compare Estonian nool), from Proto-Uralic *ńële (compare Northern Sami njuolla, Erzya нал (nal), Udmurt ньӧл (ńöl), Northern Mansi ня̄л (nâ̄l), Hungarian nyíl, Kamassian ньа (ńa)).

From Proto-Finnic *nooldak (compare Livonian nūolõ), from Proto-Uralic *ńale- (compare Northern Sami njoallut, Erzya ноламс (nolams), Eastern Mari нулаш (nulaš), Udmurt нюлыны (ńulyny), Hungarian nyal, Tundra Nenets нянсӑш (nyansăš°)).

parole.significato: to jerk (make sudden uncontrolled movements; move unsmoothly in sudden jumps)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nükidäk, from Proto-Uralic *ńüke- (“to rip, tear”) (compare Hungarian nyű).
From Proto-Finnic *nüci, from Proto-Uralic *nüδe, *niδe. Cognates include Erzya недь (neď), Hungarian nyél.

From Proto-Finnic *näktäk (compare Estonian nägema, Karelian nähä, Veps nähta), from Proto-Uralic *näke- (compare Northern Sami niegadit, Moksha няемс (näjems), Northern Mansi нэ̄глуӈкве (nè̄gluňkve), Hungarian néz). * (to see as, regard): A semantic loan from other European languages, compare Latin

From Proto-Finnic *nälkä, from Proto-Uralic *ńäle- + *-ka. Direct cognates include Estonian nälg and Northern Sami njálggis (“tasty”). Compare the bare root preserved in niellä (“to swallow”), Uralic cognate with nuolla (“to lick”).

parole.significato: thin (having little thickness or extent from one surface to its opposite)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ohut (compare Estonian õhuke, Võro ohut), probably from Proto-Uralic *wokše (compare Northern Khanty [script needed] (oχəл)).
From Proto-Finnic *oiva, probably from Proto-Uralic *ojwa (“head”) (see the Proto-Finnic entry for more).

parole.significato: to be (indicating that the subject and the complement of the verb form the same thing, or that the complement describes…
parole.testo: Most forms derive from Proto-Finnic *oldak (compare Estonian olema), from Proto-Uralic *wole- / *ole- (compare Moksha улемс (ulems), Eastern Mari улаш (ulaš), Udmurt вань (vań), Northern Khanty вөԓты (wøłty), Hungarian van, volt, and possibly Tundra Nenets ӈэсь (ŋesʹ°)); see the Proto-Uralic entry f

parole.significato: squirrel (any rodent of the family Sciuridae)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *oraba (compare Estonian orav), from Proto-Uralic *ora (compare Northern Sami oarri, Erzya ур (ur)).
From Proto-Finnic *ota (compare Estonian oda), possibly from Proto-Uralic.

From Proto-Finnic *otava, from Proto-Uralic *woča. Cognates include Karelian otava, Votic õtavõ, Ludian adam, Estonian odamus (dialectal), Erzya ош (oš, “city”). parole.significato: door (portal of entry into a building, room, or vehicle)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ouvi, possibly from Proto-Uralic *owwe.

parole.significato: burl (US), bur, burr, gnarl (tree growth in which the grain has grown in a deformed manner)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pahka, possibly from Proto-Uralic *pakša.
From Proto-Finnic *painadak, from Proto-Uralic *pańa-. * (to print (a book)): Semantic loan from Swedish trycka or German drücken.
From Proto-Finnic *paju (compare Estonian paju), from Proto-Uralic *paje-w (“willow”) (compare Udmurt бадь (baď), Hungarian fagyal (“privet”)).
From Proto-Finnic *pala (compare Estonian pala, Veps pala), from Proto-Uralic *pala (compare Erzya пал (pal), Hungarian falat (“mouthful”)).
From Proto-Finnic *paladak, from Proto-Uralic *pala-.

From Proto-Finnic *pandak (compare Estonian panema, Votic pannõ), from Proto-Uralic *pëne- (*pane-) (compare Erzya панемс (panems), Udmurt поныны (ponyny), Northern Mansi [script needed] (pin-), Tundra Nenets [script needed] (pen-)).

From Proto-Finnic *parvi, from Proto-Uralic *parewa ~ *parewe. Cognates include Estonian parv (“flock, group”), Ingrian parvi (“flock, group”), Veps parveh (“flock”), Northern Khanty пөр (pør, “flock, group”) and possibly Erzya пурнамс (purnams, “to collect, compile, gather”).
From Proto-Finnic *pata (compare Estonian pada), from Proto-Uralic *pata (compare Hungarian fazék).

parole.significato: to fear, dread, be afraid of
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pelgäit'äk, derived from Proto-Uralic *pele- of identical meaning (whence e.g. Northern Sami ballat, Erzya пелемс (pelems), Northern Mansi пилуӈкве (piluňkve) and Hungarian fél).
From Proto-Finnic *peni (compare Estonian peni), from Proto-Uralic *penä (compare Northern Sami beana, Erzya пине (pine), Eastern Mari пий (pij), Udmurt пуны (puny)).

parole.significato: rear, back, tail end (aft part of anything)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *perä (compare Estonian pära), from Proto-Uralic *perä ~ *pirä (compare Erzya пря (pŕa, “head”), Komi-Permyak бӧр (bör), Eastern Khanty пӛртӓх (pjərtäh)).
From Proto-Finnic *petägä (compare Livonian piedāg, Veps pedai), from Proto-Uralic *pecä(-kä) (compare Northern Sami beahci, Erzya пиче (piče), Eastern Mari пӱнчӧ (pünčö), Udmurt пужым (pužym)).

From Proto-Finnic *peikälo (with varying forms in descendants, such as dialectal peikalo, Karelian peikalo, Veps peigol, Estonian pöial, Livonian pēgal), probably a somewhat irregular derivation of Proto-Uralic *pelkä (compare Northern Sami bealgi, Erzya пелька (peľka, “thumb”), Komi-Zyrian пев (pev

parole.significato: jamb, post (vertical component forming the sides of a door frame, window frame or other opening in a wall)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *peeli (compare Estonian peel), from Proto-Uralic *päle (“side”) (compare Moksha пяль (päľ), Hungarian fél).
From Proto-Finnic *pimedä, from Proto-Uralic *pilmetä.
From Proto-Finnic *pitkä, derived from Proto-Uralic *pide. The comparative, superlative and many derived forms are derived from the original stem pide-.

From Proto-Finnic *poika (compare Estonian poeg, Livvi poigu), from Proto-Uralic *pojka (compare Komi-Zyrian пи (pi), Udmurt пи (pi), Northern Khanty пух (puh), Northern Mansi пыг (pyg), Hungarian fiú). The Finnic word has also been borrowed into Baltic (Latvian puika) and Swedish (see the descendan

parole.significato: knee (joint in the middle of the leg and area around it)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *polvi (compare Estonian põlv), from Proto-Uralic *polwe (compare Northern Sami buolva, Moksha пълманжа (pəlmanža)).

parole.significato: cheek (soft skin on each side of the face)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *poski, from Proto-Uralic *poske.

parole.significato: to be sick with, have, suffer from (a disease or, figuratively, a mental state)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *potëdak (compare Estonian põdema), possibly from Proto-Uralic *poče- (compare Northern Sami buohcat).
From Proto-Finnic *pouvi (compare Estonian põu), probably from Proto-Uralic *poŋŋe.

parole.significato: to fall (from an elevated position); to fall down, fall off; to drop, slip
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pudot'ak (compare Ingrian puota, Livonian pu’ddõ), probably from Proto-Uralic *puďa-w- (“to break off”) (compare Northern Sami bođˈđet, Udmurt пильыны (piľyny), Eastern Mari пудешташ (pudeštaš), Southern Mansi [script needed] (poĺ), Nganasan хоиди (hoidji)).

parole.significato: to pop, burst (of something full e.g. of gas), to rupture (e.g. of something sewn or of an abscess)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *puhkët'ak (compare Estonian puhkema, Ludian puhketa, Votic puhgõtõ), from Proto-Uralic *pučke-. The verb shares its root with putkahtaa; the root with -hk- goes back to *-šk-, which has split irregularly from *-čk- (which developed into the -tk- in putkahtaa). The same split is al

parole.significato: to speak, talk (communicate with one's voice)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *puhudak (“to blow”) (compare Estonian puhuma), from Proto-Uralic *puše- (“to blow”) (compare Northern Sami bossut, Western Mansi [script needed] (put-)). Attested since the time of Mikael Agricola (output c. 1543–1552). The semantic shift from “to blow” to “to speak” is found only

parole.significato: to intertwine, twine, twist (together) (join together by twining or twisting; join by winding around one another)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *punodak (compare Estonian punuma), from Proto-Uralic *puna- (“to spin, twist”) (compare Northern Sami botnit, Erzya понамс (ponams), Hungarian fon).
From Proto-Finnic *poola, probably from Proto-Uralic *pale (“berry”).

parole.significato: half (consisting of a half; such that two of them make one whole)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pooli (compare Estonian pool (“half”)), from Proto-Uralic *pälä (compare Northern Sami bealli, Komi-Zyrian пӧв (pöv), Northern Mansi па̄л (pāl, “half, side”), Hungarian fél (“half”), Tundra Nenets пеля (pyelya)).
From Proto-Finnic *pura, from Proto-Uralic *pura-.
From Proto-Finnic *purku, from Proto-Uralic *purke.

parole.significato: to bite (cut into something by clamping the teeth; attack with teeth)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *purdak (compare Estonian purema, Livonian pu’rrõ), from Proto-Uralic *pure- (compare Northern Sami borrat, Erzya поремс (porems), Eastern Mari пураш (puraš), Udmurt пурыны (puryny), Northern Mansi пуруӈкве (puruňkve)).
From Proto-Finnic *pusërtadak (compare Estonian puserdama, Karelian puzerdua, Veps puzerta and Votic puzõrta), probably from Proto-Uralic *puśerta-. Cognate with Hungarian facsar.

parole.significato: to pop up, turn up (to appear without warning)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *puckahtadak, derived from Proto-Uralic *pučke- (the same root as in puhjeta).

parole.significato: tube, pipe, duct, conduit (long, hollow object, often cylindrical, used to convey fluids or loose solids)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pucki (compare Estonian putk, Votic putki), from Proto-Uralic *pučke (“hollow plant stalk”) (compare Northern Sami boska (“angelica”), Erzya почко (počko, “roll, coil”), Tundra Nenets пуд (pūd)). The development from “hollow plant stalk” to “pipe, tube” is difficult to date precis
From Proto-Finnic *puu (compare Estonian puu, Karelian puu), from Proto-Uralic *puwe / *pawe (compare Eastern Mari пу (pu), Udmurt пу (pu), Hungarian fa, Tundra Nenets пя (pya)).

parole.significato: hazel grouse (Tetrastes bonasia, syn. Bonasa bonasia)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *püü (compare Estonian püü, Veps pü), from Proto-Uralic *püŋe (“hazel hen”) (compare Moksha повне (povne), Hungarian fogoly).

parole.significato: wheel (circular device capable of rotating on its axis)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pöörä, from Proto-Uralic *peŋärä.
From Proto-Finnic *päivä (“sun, day”), from Proto-Uralic *päjwä (“sun”). Cognates include Ume Sami beäjvvie, Northern Sami beaivi, Skolt Sami peiʹvv. In the sense “sun”, mostly displaced by aurinko.
From Proto-Finnic *saadak (compare Estonian saama), from Proto-Uralic *saxe- (compare Moksha самс (sams), Eastern Mari шуаш (šuaš), Komi-Zyrian суны (suny)); see it for more.

parole.significato: secret (currently used mostly idiomatically and as modifier in compound terms)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sala, from Proto-Uralic *sala (“to hide, steal, thief”). Cognates include Estonian sala (“secretly”), Livonian salātõ (“to hide something”), Northern Sami suoládit (“to keep secret, to conceal”), Northern Sami suola (“thief”), Erzya саламс (salams, “to steal”), Eastern Mari шолышт
From Proto-Finnic *salama, from Proto-Uralic *ćala-. Cognates include Southern Khanty сӑт (săt) and Eastern Mansi са̄л (sāl).

From Proto-Finnic *sarka, from Proto-Uralic *sarka (“branch?”). Cognates include Estonian sarg, Ingrian sarka, Karelian sarka, Livvi sargu, Veps sarg, Votic sarkõ, Northern Sami suorgi (“branch”), Tundra Nenets [script needed] (tārka, “branch”) and Northern Selkup [script needed] (tolka, “branch”) (

parole.significato: to precipitate (to have water in the air fall to the ground): to rain, snow, sleet, hail
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *satadak (“to fall”) (compare Estonian sadama), from Proto-Uralic *śada- (compare Southern Selkup соорогу (soorogu)), possibly borrowed from Indo-Iranian.

parole.significato: harvest, crop (natural production for a specific year, particularly of plants)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sato, probably derived from Proto-Uralic *čača- (“to grow”). Related to Erzya чачомс (čačoms, “to be born”).
From Proto-Finnic *seimi ~ *soimi, derived from Proto-Uralic *sewe-, whence syödä (“to eat”).
From Proto-Finnic *saictak (compare Estonian seisma, Võro saisma), from Proto-Uralic *sańśa- ~ *säńśä-.

From Proto-Finnic *säic'en (compare Estonian seitse (“seven”)), from Proto-Uralic *ćäjćemä (*śäjćemä) (compare Erzya сисем (sisem, “seven”), Eastern Mari шым (šym), Udmurt сизьым (śiźym), Tundra Nenets сӣˮив (syīqyiw°)). The original nominative form (seitsen) has been largely displaced by the geniti

From Proto-Finnic *seka, possibly from Proto-Uralic *sekä (“inside, interior”), thus "among" (also see seassa) and later "mixed". The word has (presumably original) front vowels in Võro but back vowels elsewhere.
From Proto-Finnic *sepä (“neck”), from Proto-Uralic *śepä (“neck”). Cognates include Erzya сиве (sive).
From Proto-Finnic *setä, from Proto-Uralic *čečä (*śečä) (compare Northern Sami čeahci, Eastern Mari [script needed] (čüčü), Northern Mansi [script needed] (sasi̮γ)).
From Proto-Finnic *sii, possibly from Proto-Uralic *śiŋe.

From Proto-Finnic *silmä (compare Estonian silm), from Proto-Uralic *śilmä (compare Northern Sami čalbmi, Erzya сельме (seľme), Eastern Mari шинча (šinča), Udmurt син (śin), Northern Mansi сам (sam), Northern Khanty сєм (sêm), Hungarian szem, Tundra Nenets сэв (sew°)).

parole.significato: you (second-person singular personal pronoun, used in familiar or neutral contexts), thou
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *cinä, from Proto-Uralic *tinä. See the Proto-Finnic entry for more information on inflection.

parole.significato: common lizard, viviparous lizard, Zootoca vivipara
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sisalikko (compare Estonian sisalik, Karelian čičiliušku), likely from Proto-Uralic (see the Proto-Finnic entry for more).
From Proto-Finnic *sitta, possibly from Proto-Uralic *sitta.
From Proto-Finnic *soimat'ak, from Proto-Uralic *śojma (compare soida). Cognate with Estonian sõimama.
From Proto-Finnic *sonsar, possibly from Proto-Uralic *ćonča, *ćoča.
From Proto-Finnic *sopa (compare Estonian sõba, Votic sõpa), from Proto-Uralic *śopa. In the sense “garment, piece of clothing”, displaced by vaate.

parole.significato: war (conflict involving organized use of arms; also figuratively, e.g. of a campaign against something or business comp…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sota (compare Estonian sõda, Livonian suodā, Veps soda, Võro sõda), from Proto-Uralic *śoďa (compare Erzya сюдома (śudoma, “to curse”), Eastern Mari шудалаш (šudalaš, “to curse”), Tundra Nenets сайнорць (saynorcʹ°, “to be at war”)).

parole.significato: to row (propel over water using oars)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *soutadak, from Proto-Uralic *suxta-.

parole.significato: ski (one of a pair of long flat runners designed for gliding over snow, ice or water)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *suksi, from Proto-Uralic *sukse. Cognate with Erzya сокс (soks).

parole.significato: to melt, thaw (change from a solid state to a liquid state, usually by a gradual heat)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *suladak, from Proto-Uralic *sula- (compare Moksha соламс (solams), Eastern Mari шулаш (šulaš), Komi-Permyak сывны (syvny), Southern Khanty тӑтә (tătə), Hungarian olvad).

parole.significato: feather, more specifically a flight feather (stiff feather in a bird's wing or tail used in flying)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sulka, probably from Proto-Uralic *tulka (see the Proto-Finnic entry for details). Cognates include Estonian sulg, Erzya толга (tolga) and Hungarian toll.
From Proto-Finnic *sooli (compare Estonian sool), from Proto-Uralic *śale (compare Northern Sami čoalli, Erzya сюло (śulo), Udmurt сюл (śul)).

parole.significato: scale (one of the keratin pieces covering the skin of certain animals)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *soomu(s) (compare Estonian soomus, Veps somuz), from Proto-Uralic *śëme (compare Erzya сяв (śav), Udmurt сьӧм (śöm), Komi-Permyak сьӧм (śöm)).

parole.significato: vessel, vas (tube or canal that carries fluid)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sooni, from Proto-Uralic *sëne. Cognates include Estonian soon, Erzya сан (san), Northern Mansi та̄н (tān), Hungarian ín (“sinew”).

parole.significato: violent or accidental death (mainly used of humans)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *surma, from Proto-Uralic *śurma. Equivalent to surra + -ma (although the original meaning of surra, “to die”, is not found in Finnish). Cognates include Estonian surm, Karelian šurma.

parole.significato: to mourn, grieve (often because of someone's death)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *surdak (“to die”) (compare Estonian surema (“to die”)), from Proto-Uralic *śure- (“to die”). The modern meaning is by contamination from surku; the original meaning is still found in the derivative surma (“killing”). May also be related to Erzya сырьмай (sïŕmaj, “death”).
From Proto-Finnic *suu (compare Estonian suu), from Proto-Uralic *śuwe (compare Northern Mansi сӯп (sūp), Hungarian száj, Tundra Nenets сё (syo)).

From Proto-Finnic *suvi, from Proto-Uralic *suŋe (compare Northern Sami sakŋat (“be thawed”), Nganasan тәӈәә (təŋəə)). Replaced in the standard language in the 19th century with kesä, which was traditionally used in the eastern dialects (as opposed to suvi, which was traditionally a Western Finnish

From Proto-Finnic *südän (compare Estonian süda), from Proto-Uralic *śüdäme (compare Skolt Sami čââʹđ, Erzya седей (sedej), Eastern Mari шӱм (šüm), Komi-Zyrian сьӧлӧм (śölöm), Northern Mansi сым (sym), Hungarian szív, Tundra Nenets сей (syey°)).

parole.significato: arms (in reference to embracing or holding in both one's arms)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *süli, from Proto-Uralic *süle. Cognates include Estonian süli, Veps sülʹ, Erzya сэль (sëľ, “fathom”), Hungarian öl.
From Proto-Finnic *sülkedäk, from Proto-Uralic *ćülke-.
From Proto-Finnic *süntüdäk (compare Estonian sündima), from Proto-Uralic *sentew- (compare Nganasan тынтуди (tyntudji)).
From Proto-Finnic *süci (compare Estonian süsi), from Proto-Uralic *ćüďe (compare Erzya седь (seď)).

From Proto-Finnic *süü (compare Estonian süü), from Proto-Uralic *siwe (compare Eastern Mari ший (šij), Komi-Zyrian сі (si), Tundra Nenets [script needed] (t̜́ì)). The sense “reason, cause” (and those akin to it) was originally figurative, and is also found elsewhere in Finnic.
From Proto-Finnic *süklä (compare Karelian syplä, Votic sügle), probably from Proto-Uralic *śüklä (compare Erzya сильге (siľge)).
From Proto-Finnic *söödäk (compare Estonian sööma), from Proto-Uralic *sewe- (compare Erzya сэвемс (sëvems), Udmurt сины (śiny), Northern Mansi тэ̄ӈкве (tè̄ňkve), Hungarian eszik).

From Proto-Finnic *säkä, from Proto-Uralic *śäkᴈ ~ *śekᴈ. Related to Estonian säga, Erzya сие (sije), Moksha сия (sijä), Eastern Mari ший (šij), Eastern Khanty сәг (səg), Southern Khanty сәҳ (səḥ) and Northern Mansi сиг (sig).

parole.significato: to place a burden or load, to lump, to saddle
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sälüttädäk, probably from Proto-Uralic *sälä-.
From Proto-Finnic *sänki (compare Veps säng), possibly from Proto-Uralic (see the Proto-Finnic entry for more).

parole.significato: this, that (medial between tämä and tuo)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *taa, from Proto-Uralic *ta.
From Proto-Finnic *taka, from Proto-Uralic *taka.

parole.significato: to lead (guide or conduct in a certain course, especially assertively; a child, dog etc.)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *taluttadak. Equivalent to talua + -ttaa (from a dialectal verb talua), from Proto-Finnic *taludak, probably from Proto-Uralic *talwa-.
From Proto-Finnic *talvi (compare Estonian talv), from Proto-Uralic *tälwä (compare Erzya теле (tele), Western Mari тел (tel), Udmurt тол (tol), Northern Mansi та̄л (tāl), Hungarian tél).
From Proto-Finnic *tappadak, from Proto-Uralic *tappa- (compare Erzya тапамс (tapams), Tundra Nenets тӑпӑрць (tăpărcʹ°)).

parole.significato: to (be able to) withstand the cold, be warm enough (in order not to shiver with cold)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tarkëdak + -eta (compare Estonian targema, Ingrian tareta), from Proto-Uralic *tarke- (“to shiver, tremble”).

parole.significato: even, equal, equi-, homo-, flat, uniform
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tasa, possibly from Proto-Uralic *taśa.

parole.significato: you (second-person plural; when addressing many persons or when addressing politely or formally one person)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tek, from Proto-Uralic *te. The word is inflected as plural, but there is no plural marker in the nominative, except in dialects (tet).
From Proto-Finnic *tora, from Proto-Uralic *tora. Cognates include Erzya тюрема (ťurema, “fight, war”).
From Proto-Finnic *toci (compare Estonian tõsi), from Proto-Uralic *čoďe (compare Eastern Khanty [script needed] (čăjǝ), Northern Mansi [script needed] (sōĺ)).
From Proto-Finnic *touko (compare Estonian tõug), probably from Proto-Uralic (see the Proto-Finnic entry for more).

From Proto-Finnic *tuli (compare Estonian tuli), from Proto-Uralic *tule (compare Northern Sami dolla, Moksha тол (tol), Eastern Mari тул (tul), Udmurt тыл (tyl), Tundra Nenets ту (tu)). tuli has previously been typical of Eastern Finnish, whereas Western Finnish dialects usually used valkea.

From Proto-Finnic *tuntëdak (compare Estonian tundma), from Proto-Uralic *tumte- (compare Northern Sami dovdat, Komi-Zyrian тӧдны (tödny), Hungarian tud, Tundra Nenets тумдӑсь (tumdăsʹ°)).

parole.significato: that (over there) (compare se, see usage notes)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *too, from Proto-Uralic *to (compare Erzya тона (tona), Hungarian tova). Attested since the time of Mikael Agricola (output c. 1543–1552), but only once in all of Agricola's works (for comparison, tämä is attested nearly two thousand times and se over ten thousand times).

parole.significato: to bring, fetch, get (transport toward somebody/somewhere)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *toodak (compare Estonian tooma), from Proto-Uralic *toxe- (compare Erzya туемс (tujems), Northern Khanty [script needed] (tu-)); see it for more.

parole.significato: bird cherry, hackberry, hagberry, Prunus padus (tree)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *toomi (compare Estonian toom), from Proto-Uralic *ďëme (compare Northern Sami duopma, Erzya лём (ľom), Eastern Mari ломбо (lombo), Komi-Zyrian льӧм (ľöm), Northern Mansi ля̄м (lâ̄m), Kamassian лем (lem)).
From Proto-Finnic *tümä, from Proto-Uralic *ďümä. Displaced by the borrowed liima.

parole.significato: foot (lowest part of a longish object, e.g. a tree)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tüvi (compare Estonian tüvi), from Proto-Uralic *tüŋe (compare Eastern Mari тӱҥ (tüŋ), Hungarian tő).
From Proto-Finnic *täi (compare Estonian täi), from Proto-Uralic *täje (compare Eastern Mari ти (ti), Komi-Permyak той (toj), Udmurt тэй (tej), Hungarian tetű).
From Proto-Finnic *tämä, from Proto-Uralic *tä. The nominative and singular genitive forms, which would have otherwise been monosyllabic, have been extended with *-mä.
From Proto-Finnic *tävü, from Proto-Uralic *täwe(w). Cognates include Erzya тевеляв (teveľav). Displaced by keuhko.

From Proto-Finnic *täüci (compare Estonian täis), from Proto-Uralic *täwde (compare Northern Sami dievas, Eastern Mari тич (tič), Eastern Khanty тӓԓә (täłə), Hungarian tele, Tundra Nenets тер (tyer°)).

parole.significato: to swim (move through water without touching the bottom)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *uidak, from Proto-Uralic *o(w)je- ~ *uje-. Cognate to Estonian ujuma, Ter Sami vɨjjed, Erzya уемс (ujems) and Hungarian úszik.

From Proto-Finnic *vaimo (“spirit, soul”) (compare Estonian vaim (“spirit”)), possibly derived from Proto-Uralic *wajŋe (“(living) spirit”) (compare Northern Sami vuoigŋa (“breath, spirit”), Moksha вайме (vajme), Erzya ойме (ojme, “spirit, soul”), Nganasan бачуˮ (bačuʔ, “soul”)). The original sense
From Proto-Finnic *vala, from Proto-Uralic *wala (compare Lule Sami vuolle, Erzya вал (val, “word”), Nganasan бәлы (bəly)).
From Proto-Finnic *vanha (compare Estonian vana), from Proto-Uralic *wanša (compare Komi-Zyrian важ (važ), Udmurt вуж (vuž)).

parole.significato: hooded crow, grey crow, Corvus cornix
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *varis, from Proto-Uralic *warᴈ. Cognates include Estonian vares, Veps variš, Karelian varis, Erzya варака (varaka), Moksha варси (varsi) and Hungarian varjú. Likely an onomatopoeic word, compare Russian воро́на (voróna).
From Proto-Finnic *vasën, from Proto-Uralic *wasa (originally with the comparative suffix -mpi).

From Proto-Finnic *vaski, from Proto-Uralic *wäśkä ~ *waśke. Cognate with Estonian vask, Erzya уське (uśke) and Hungarian vas. Originally meant “copper” in a broad sense; displaced later by borrowings (e.g. kupari (“copper”), pronssi (“bronze”), messinki (“brass”)) in practically all of these senses
From Proto-Finnic *veci (compare Estonian vesi), from Proto-Uralic *wete (compare Erzya ведь (veď), Eastern Mari вӱд (vüd), Udmurt ву (vu), Hungarian víz, Tundra Nenets иˮ (yiq)).

parole.significato: to take away, take, bring away
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *veedäk (compare Estonian viima), from Proto-Uralic *wixe- (compare Skolt Sami viikkâd, Erzya виемс (vijems), Hungarian visz, Northern Selkup ӱ̄ӄо (ǖqo)).

Metathesized form of Proto-Finnic *viherä, derived by -rä from Proto-Uralic *wiša (see *viha). Further etymology and cognates. From Proto-Finnic *viici (compare Estonian viis), from Proto-Uralic *witte (compare Erzya вете (vete), Northern Khanty вет (wjet), Northern Mansi ат (at), Hungarian öt, Nganasan бииˮ (biiʔ, “ten”)).

parole.significato: to scutch, swingle (to beat or flog for extracting the fibers from flax stalks)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vitodak, from Proto-Uralic *wiča-.
From Proto-Finnic *voo, from Proto-Uralic *wuwa (“current, flow”).

parole.significato: to carve, whittle (wood or a similar material)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vooldak, from Proto-Uralic *wale-.

parole.significato: mountain (large mass of earth and rock)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *voori, from Proto-Uralic *wëre ~ *ware (compare Udmurt выр (vyr)). Compare vaara, a Sami borrowing possibly from the same Uralic root.
From Proto-Finnic *vooci, from Proto-Uralic *ëde.
From Proto-Finnic *vävü, from Proto-Uralic *wäŋew, cognate to e.g. Estonian väi, Northern Sami vivva, Hungarian vő, Veps vävu and Nganasan биӈи (biŋi).

From Proto-Finnic *ükci (compare Estonian üks), from Proto-Uralic *ükte (compare Northern Sami okta, Erzya вейке (vejke), Eastern Mari ик (ik), Udmurt одӥг (odig), Northern Mansi акв (akv), аква (akva)).

parole.significato: over [with genitive] (to or through the space that is above something)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *üli, from Proto-Uralic *üle (compare Northern Sami ala, Erzya вель- (veľ-), вельга (veľga), Western Mari вӹлӓн (vÿlän), Udmurt выл (vyl), Northern Khanty єԓ (êł), Tundra Nenets ниʼ (nyih)).
From Proto-Finnic *ülkä, possibly from Proto-Uralic *ülkä (“boy, son”) (cognate with Proto-Samic *ëlkē).

From Proto-Finnic *öö (compare Estonian öö, Karelian yö, Livonian īe), from Proto-Uralic *üje ~ *eje (compare Northern Sami idja, Inari Sami ijjâ, Moksha ве (ve), Udmurt уй (uj), Komi-Zyrian вой (voj), Southern Mansi йӣ (jī), Hungarian éj).

According to Ante Aikio (2020), from Proto-Finnic *äisäk (compare Estonian äsja, Ludian äskei, Võro äisäq), from Proto-Uralic *äńćä. This suggests a development from *äisäk > *äisäk(k)V- > *äiskV- > *eskV-/äskV-.
